comment: without MODE_HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE, NOT is NOT_SYM
find_keyword rewrites NOT_SYM to NOT2_SYM under MODE_HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE
the rewrite happens after the case-insensitive lookup
the rewrite is keyed on the *token* NOT_SYM, so '!' (a character token) is untouched - gen_lex_token.cc's set_token(NOT2_SYM, "!") is digest text, not a lexeme (PLAN.md 1.2, G.0 caveat)
default: '||' is OR2_SYM
MODE_PIPES_AS_CONCAT without MODE_ORACLE -> MYSQL_CONCAT_SYM (the ORACLE_CONCAT_SYM arm needs MODE_ORACLE, ignored)
even with ORACLE in the mode string the MariaDB arm is taken: ORACLE is recognised and ignored (D-8)
ANSI_QUOTES: '"' delimits identifiers
default: '"' delimits strings
a doubled backslash is two bytes either way
with NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES the literal ends at the third quote
without the mode the backslash escapes the quote and the fourth character closes the literal
IGNORE_SPACE lets a sql_functions[] keyword be followed by spaces then '('
without it, SUM is an identifier
the skip loop counts newlines as space too

with a space before the '.', scan_ident_middle's 'start == get_ptr()' test fails under IGNORE_SPACE and c is '.' only after the skip loop; either way MY_LEX_IDENT_SEP is reached through MY_LEX_REAL_OR_POINT with a space as the follower, so next_state is MY_LEX_START and 'b' comes back from scan_ident_middle as IDENT_QUOTED, not the IDENT that 'a.b' gives
two flags at once
the MODE_ORACLE keyword table (BEGIN_ORACLE_SYM etc.) is ignored by D-8
COLON_ORACLE_SYM is not emitted: ORACLE is ignored
the ORACLE rewrite MINUS_ORACLE_SYM -> EXCEPT_SYM is not applied
'.b' with no space after the dot: MY_LEX_IDENT_SEP sees an ident byte, sets MY_LEX_IDENT_OR_QUALIFIED_SPECIAL_FUNC, and scan_ident_common returns a 7-bit IDENT

D-8/P10: a `SET sql_mode` that is the *first* statement of the input takes effect on the next one. Until P10 src/scanner.c could not see it — the forward look needs a produced token in front of the SET and a document that opens with one has none — so this row is the regression pin for that repair; the reference side follows the same SET (sqlmode_track.TrackingReflex) and the C side is driven from tree-sitter's empty external state (lexdump --doc-start).

the SET statement is lexed under the *old* mode, so its own "ANSI_QUOTES" is still a TEXT_STRING while the next statement's "x" is an identifier: thd->variables.sql_mode is written when the SET executes, after its own statement has been lexed.

the same leading SET carrying IGNORE_SPACE: `SUM (` is the sql_functions[] keyword across the space only because the mode reached the second statement. This is the reading evidence/P9/sql-mode-followon.json measured as broken.
the third flag a leading SET has to carry into find_keyword(): NOT becomes NOT2_SYM only under MODE_HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE.
`SET SESSION sql_mode = ...` — the scope keyword form of D-8, from the head of the document.

`SET @@session.sql_mode = ...` — the @@-qualified form, from the head of the document. None of `@`, `session`, `.` or `sql_mode` is an external token, so the anchor the scanner uses here is the word SET itself.
`sql_mode = ''` resets (D-8), and the second SET is found by the ordinary forward look from the `;` that ends the first — so the third statement's "x" is a TEXT_STRING again.
the negative: `sql_modes` is not `sql_mode`, so nothing changes and "x" stays a TEXT_STRING. Both engines have to agree on the miss as well as on the hit.

the negative D-8's document-start look is narrowed by (P10 round 2): the server applies a `SET sql_mode` only where a statement may begin, and this `SET` is the assignment list of an UPDATE. `src/scanner.c` reaches that word before any external token has been produced — the same window a leading SET is found in — and must not move the mode there; the byte-0 condition on the look is what keeps it out. Both engines say `"x"` is still a TEXT_STRING.
sql:
UPDATE mysql.proc SET sql_mode='ANSI_QUOTES';
SELECT "x" FROM t
